reviews.title: Admirable performance for the cost, but it is tall
reviews.comment: TLDR: you can get better cooling from an AIO, but the price and performance of this tower perfect for your average user on a budget. Make sure it fits in your case. The mounting system is secure and makes good contact with the CPU die. The included thermal compound is good enough to not require another purchase as well. My issue with the mounting bracket was that it required more force than I anticipated to align the screws and I had to remount the cooler to ensure even pressure because I had missed that one screw was not threaded into the bracket. - perhaps it could have used slightly taller standoffs. Otherwise installation was easy and the fan mount looks nicer than clips would for this styling. RGB is bright and the selection of colors and modes are fun. I appreciate that I can pick a plain white light or just leave it off. In terms of performance, I see ~20C difference above ambient from my stock cooler (wraith stealth) and the noise is potentially blower under load depending on your fan curve. Under heavy load with a slight OC my temps are stable below 75C and idle around 35C. The main downside to look out for is it's height from the GPU. My case is wide and accommodates the cooler, but if you have a narrow case I would look for another solution.

reviews.title: Sturdy and Effective Cooling with Appealing Aesthetics
reviews.comment: This fan was selected for use in my new desktop computer, and my experience with it thus far has been positive. It looks good, with attractive color accents that enhance the overall appearance of my new desktop. Beyond aesthetics, the fan exhibits a robust and sturdy construction, instilling confidence in its long-term durability. Most importantly, it performs well, and moves a lot of air, which is crucial for maintaining optimal system performance. The fan's sturdy build is a notable advantage, suggesting resilience and longevity. Additionally, the appealing color scheme adds a welcome visual element to the computer's internal components. Its capacity to move a substantial amount of air is a critical pro, ensuring efficient cooling and contributing to the overall stability and performance of the system. At this time, no drawbacks have been identified. In conclusion, this fan proves to be a solid choice for a computer build, offering a combination of effective cooling performance, durable construction, and pleasing visual design. Its ability to move a significant volume of air, coupled with its sturdiness and attractive colors, makes it an excellent choice.
reviews.author: Tommy Amos

reviews.title: This product is amazing.
reviews.comment: So prior to this purchase I bought a msi mag 240mm(garbage). Troubleshot this AIO for 2 months before finally rma'ing it at the time of posting this. Playing games was 80+, prime95 tests/cinebench 80-90c and specifically destiny two sometimes I'd see 93c, apex 75-85c. I installed the 212 black argb last night. The temps are absolutely amazing. Once I played for about an hour to get an accurate reading I didn't even hit 70c most of the time i was under 60c even at 100% cpu loadwith this thing on my 5600x at stock with a -25 curve. Bang for buck this product is amazing especially when it is on sale, it is a huge value and works amazing for a 65w chip. Only thing that sucked was the mount on the back of the motherboard. I had to take 8 or 9 screw out of my motherboard to get enough clearance for the bottom left screw on the backplate. It wasn't hard just an extra step. The fan is not addressable rgb(which I am just going to replace it). I just used the little switch it comes with for the time being. If you add another fan for a push/pull I'd imagine temps would drop a little lower even. If you're like me and research until your crazy on pc parts. Just buy this thing. Just make sure you're not on a like 12900k it won't cool super high wattage cpus but for mids like the 5600x. Absolutely amazing. 1 weird thing I want to add just in case anyone else has this issue. First boot up even with the stock fan plugged into the cpu fan pwm. I got "cpu fan error!" The workaround for this is just to turn off the monitor on the cpu fan in bios. Super weird, I didn't care much since I am replacing that fan anyways, but just so you know! Even if you disable the monitoring of the fan, works fine
